learn.intro: Hi! Lesson 6 — **Flexbox**. Before, designers struggled with float and hacks to align blocks. Now you say how to arrange elements and the browser lays them out. Let's go!

slides.text: The main idea: there is a **container** (the parent) and **items** inside it. We set up the container and the items adapt themselves.
Without Flexbox `div` blocks stand one under another. Add `display: flex` to the parent — and they line up **in a row**:
The elements inside the container are called **flex items**.

check.prompt: Where do you write display: flex?
check.explain: Flex is turned on at the container.

check.prompt: Elements inside a flex container are called flex items.
check.explain: The container is the parent, the items are the children.

slides.text:
A container has a **main axis** — the direction the items line up in.
`row` (default) — in a row, left to right.
`column` — one under another, top to bottom.

check.prompt: What is the default value of flex-direction?
check.explain: row — in a row, left to right.

slides.text: `justify-content` moves items **along** the main axis. For `row` that is horizontal, for `column` — vertical.

`flex-start` — to the start, `center` — centered, `flex-end` — to the end.
`space-between` — the first at the start, the last at the end, equal gaps between.
`space-around` — equal space around each (half a gap at the edges).
`space-between` is the most common choice for a menu: logo on the left, links on the right.

check.prompt: Which value puts the logo on the left and the links on the right?
check.explain: space-between pushes the end items to the edges.

check.prompt: Match the value and the result

slides.text: `align-items` moves items **across** the main axis. For `row` that is vertical. To see the difference we give the container a height:
`flex-start` — to the top, `center` — centered, `flex-end` — to the bottom, `stretch` (default) — stretched to the full height.
A memory trick: `justify` — «**j**ust along», `align` — «**a**cross». For `row`: justify-content moves **left-right**, align-items — **up-down**.

check.prompt: What moves items up and down with flex-direction: row?
justify-content moves items along the main axis.

slides.text: A navigation menu: logo on the left, links on the right, everything centered vertically:

Homework: a profile card — **avatar on the left**, **name and description on the right**, all centered vertically. Give the parent `display: flex` and `align-items: center`, the avatar a fixed width, for example `width: 80px`.

check.prompt: What does the profile card parent need to center everything vertically?

questions.prompt: What happens after display: flex on the parent?
options: The blocks line up in a row
questions.explain: Items line up along the main axis.

questions.prompt: We set up the container and the items inside adapt themselves.
questions.explain: That is the main idea of Flexbox.

questions.prompt: How are items placed with space-between?
options: The first at the start, the last at the end, equal gaps between
questions.explain: This is the most common choice for a menu.

pairs: Ends at the edges, equal gaps between

questions.prompt: What is the default value of align-items?
Which property centers items vertically with row?
questions.explain: align-items works across the main axis.

questions.prompt: Which property moves items along the main axis? (one hyphenated word)
Why give the container a height when trying align-items?
questions.explain: Without a height there is no free space across the axis.

questions.prompt: Build the menu rule: logo left, links right, centered vertically
questions.explain: Flex, spread to edges and vertical center.

questions.prompt: Which three properties make the menu from the practice?
questions.explain: A flex container plus two alignments.

questions.prompt: For a profile card the avatar should get a fixed width, for example 80px.
questions.explain: Then the text on the right takes the rest of the space.
